sourceFlowReconstruction: L1-7 Mishnah: seven days before Yom Kippur the Kohen Gadol is separated from his house to the Parhedrin chamber; another kohen is prepared in his place lest a disqualification befall him. R. Yehuda: also another wife is prepared lest his wife die, as it says 'vekhipper ba'ado uve'ad beito', beito = his wife. They said to him: if so there is no end to the matter. (Hebrew Rashi: pesul = keri or other tumah barring entry to the Mikdash; ein ladavar sof = perhaps this one too will die.)

L8-14 Gemara: tenan hatam - seven days before burning the parah the kohen who burns it was separated from his house to the chamber facing the Bira, north-east, called Lishkat Beit HaEven. Why the name? All its acts (Rashi: of the parah) are in dung, stone and earth vessels.

L14-20: mai ta'ama? Since a tevul yom is fit for the parah - ditnan they would make the kohen who burns the parah tamei and immerse him, to remove from the heart of the Sadducees who said it was done by me'orvei shemesh - the Rabbis instituted for it dung/stone/earth vessels that do not receive tumah, so that they not treat it lightly.

L20-24: why north-east? Since it is a chatat and a chatat requires north, and it is written of it 'el nokhach pnei ohel moed', the Rabbis instituted for it a north-east chamber so that it have a hekera. (Rashi: altar chataot are slaughtered in the north, not that this one requires north, it is slaughtered on Har HaMishchah; the verse is at the sprinkling, he faces the Heichal entrance in the eastern wall; hekera = to know he was separated there for the parah service called chatat and requiring east, and set his heart to be diligent.)

L24-27: mai Bira? Rabba bar bar Chana in the name of R. Yochanan: a place on the Temple Mount named Bira. Reish Lakish: the whole Mikdash is called Bira, as it says 'haBira asher hakhinoti' (Rashi: David says this verse in Chronicles). No decision stated.

L27-38: mena hanei milei? R. Minyomi bar Chilkiya in the name of R. Machseya bar Idi in the name of R. Yochanan: 'ka'asher asah bayom hazeh tzivah Hashem la'asot lekhaper aleikhem' - la'asot = acts of parah, lekhaper = acts of Yom Kippur (Rashi: said at the milu'im, when they were commanded to separate from their homes seven days and served on the eighth). Granted the whole verse cannot be about parah, lekhaper is written and parah is not for atonement; but say the whole verse is about Yom Kippur? They say: learn tzivah-tzivah; here 'tzivah Hashem la'asot', there 'zot chukat haTorah asher tzivah Hashem lemor'; as there parah so here parah, as here separation so there separation.
L39: 've'eima' - a further 'but say' begins; the daf ends physically here. Whether the derivation stands is OPEN at the end of 2a.

defects.fieldSays: the Sages chose it 'so that the chamber would have a distinguishing sign'
defects.sourceSupports: 'תקינו לה רבנן לשכה צפונה מזרחה כי היכי דלהוי לה היכירא': both 'לה' continue the parah as subject (as in L18 'תקינו לה רבנן כלי גללים'); Rashi explains the hekera as making known that the kohen was separated for the parah service called chatat. The source does not say the chamber has the sign; the chamber's location IS the sign, for the parah. Resolving the pronoun to 'the chamber' points it at the wrong subject. Every other field in the record keeps the neutral 'it'.
defects.suggestedRepair: '...so that it would have a distinguishing sign' (or 'so that the parah would have').
